title: When More Evidence Hurts: Publication-Bias Drift and Principled Stopping for Biomedical Causal Search
abstract: arXiv:2609.24101v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Automated biomedical evidence synthesis depends on retrieving published studies, but the biomedical literature is systematically skewed toward positive findings. Deeper retrieval can therefore make a system \emph{more} likely to falsely infer benefit when the true effect is null. We formalise this phenomenon as \emph{evidence drift} and prove that, under a standard publication-bias model, the false-positive probability on null-effect queries follows a strictly increasing large-sample envelope in retrieval depth, approaching one. Empirically, on a held-out test set of 140 Cochrane-derived queries, drift rises monotonically from 7.9\% to 15.7\% as the retrieval budget grows from 3 to 20 steps, and concentrates in the null-effect class. We present DACG-agent, a drift-aware causal-graph agent that incrementally builds a causal knowledge graph from PubMed abstracts and applies a two-layer stopping policy with complementary roles: a KL-diver

translated_title: 当更多证据反而有害时：生物医学因果检索中的发表偏倚漂移与有原则的停止策略
translated_abstract: 自动化的生物医学证据合成依赖于检索已发表的研究，但生物医学文献系统性地偏向阳性结果。因此，当真实效应为零时，更深入的检索反而可能使系统更容易错误地推断出存在有益效果。我们将这一现象形式化为“证据漂移”（evidence drift），并证明在标准的发表偏倚模型下，零效应查询的假阳性概率随检索深度遵循一个严格递增的大样本包络，并趋近于一。在实证方面，在一个由140个源自Cochrane的查询组成的保留测试集上，随着检索预算从3步增加到20步，漂移从7.9%单调上升至15.7%，且集中在零效应类别中。我们提出了DACG-agent，一种漂移感知的因果图智能体，它从PubMed摘要中增量式地构建因果知识图谱，并应用具有互补作用的双层停止策略：一个基于KL散度……
tldr: 该论文揭示并形式化了“证据漂移”现象——由于发表偏倚，检索更多文献反而会提高零效应场景下的假阳性率，并提出漂移感知的因果图智能体DACG-agent，通过有原则的双层停止策略来决定何时停止检索。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes "evidence drift"—where publication bias causes deeper retrieval to increase false-positive rates on null-effect queries—and proposes DACG-agent, a drift-aware causal-graph agent with a principled two-layer stopping policy.
